title: Projectile motion; Systems and center of mass
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics 1 (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: D07-ap1#t1 term and clue written for the game; D07-ap1#t2 term and clue written for the game; K04-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; K04-1#t4 term and clue written for the game. assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: System
items.clue: The collection of objects you choose to study.

items.label: Environment
items.clue: Everything other than the objects you have chosen to study.

items.label: Range
items.clue: Horizontal distance a projectile covers between launch and landing.

items.label: Horizontal component
items.clue: Part of the launch velocity that never changes, as no force acts that way.

questions.stem: A cylindrical rod is made of a 0.50 m aluminium section joined end to end to a 0.50 m steel section of the same diameter. Each section is uniform, and the steel section has the greater mass. How does the location of the rod's centre of mass compare with the rod's midpoint?

options.text: It is at the midpoint, since the rod's shape is symmetric about that point.
It is on the aluminium side of the midpoint, nearer the lighter section.
It is at the centre of the steel section, the more massive part.
It lies between the midpoint and the centre of the steel section.

questions.stem: Logs burn in an open fireplace. Smoke and hot gases rise up the chimney, and a little ash is left behind. The system is the logs and whatever remains of them in the fireplace. Which statement about the mass of this system is correct?

options.text: It stays constant, since mass is conserved in every physical and chemical change.
It stays constant, since the gases that leave the fireplace have no mass of their own.
It decreases, as the gases produced carry mass across the system's boundary.
It decreases, as the burning destroys the wood's matter and its mass disappears.

questions.stem: A uniform rod of mass 2m and length L has a small ball of mass m fixed to one end. How far from the other end of the rod is the centre of mass of the rod–ball system?

A student wants to find the time Earth takes to orbit the Sun once. The student models Earth, with its oceans, its atmosphere and its slowly churning interior, as a single object. Which evaluation of this modeling choice is correct?

options.text: Appropriate: the orbital period depends only on how Earth moves as a whole.
Not appropriate: Earth is much too large to be treated as one single object.
Not appropriate: Earth's oceans, air and interior move relative to one another.
Appropriate: any system can be modeled as a single object, whatever the question.

questions.stem: A diver makes two dives from the same springboard. In each dive, her center of mass leaves the board from the same height with the same velocity. In dive 1 she keeps her body straight; in dive 2 she pulls into a tight tuck soon after leaving the board. Air resistance is negligible. How do the maximum heights reached by her center of mass in the two dives compare?

options.text: Dive 2's is greater, since pulling into a tuck lifts her body higher.
They cannot be compared, since a rotating object is not a projectile.
They are equal, since her center of mass moves as a projectile in both dives.
Dive 1's is greater, since her outstretched body reaches higher.

questions.stem: A person of mass m stands at one end of a uniform raft of mass 4m and length L. The raft floats at rest on still water, and the water exerts a negligible horizontal force on it. The person walks to the other end of the raft and stops. How far does the raft move relative to the water?
